hypothesis: The --experimental-router public regression documented in router_ablation_results.json (0.95365 -> 0.95355) is caused by a single identifiable session, and equal-weight RRF fusion of BM25 and dense ranks is the specific mechanism.

root_cause_trace.method: Diffed per-session first_hit_turn/best_rank between the default agent and --experimental-router (with dense installed) on the public set; exactly one session differed.
root_cause_trace.explanation: The target is a decisive BM25 leader (rank 1) for a narrow, specific category phrase, but the MiniLM dense encoder does not retrieve it in its own top 200. Equal-weight RRF still lets competitor products that rank moderately on both BM25 and dense out-score a BM25-only leader, because RRF sums independent per-source terms rather than protecting a confident single-source winner. Product-group diversity bucketing then compounds the demotion further, though the miss at output_limit=1 is already determined by the fusion step alone.

change: Added an optional dense_rrf_weight parameter (Agent constructor, --dense-rrf-weight CLI flag on run_solution.py and stress_eval.py) that scales the dense term in the intra-route RRF sum: rrf = 1/(60+bm25_rank) + dense_rrf_weight/(60+dense_rank). Default remains 1.0 (no behavior change to any existing documented result). At weight 0.0, dense retrieval still contributes candidates to the pool (recall) but no longer influences ranking order, so a decisive BM25 leader can no longer be displaced by fusion.

public.note: public_0134 hits at turn 1 rank 1 (same as baseline) only at weight 0.0; weights 0.2-0.8 still miss at turn 1 despite the target's fused rank improving monotonically with lower weight (43 -> 34 -> 23 -> 17 -> 11 -> 8 -> 7 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 at weight 0.0), because output_limit=1 requires an exact rank-1 match on early turns.

stress.note: Router was never regressed on stress; weight change has no effect either direction.

asin_separated_validation_400.note: Router+dense already trails the deterministic default by ~0.00005-0.0001 here regardless of weight (likely noise at n=400); weight 0.0 is marginally worse than weight 1.0 on this split, the opposite direction from the public-set effect.

reason: dense_rrf_weight=0.0 fully and reproducibly eliminates the one known public regression with zero cost on stress, so it is a strict improvement to the --experimental-router path specifically on the public promotion gate. It does not, however, make --experimental-router beat the deterministic default on the ASIN-separated validation set, so this does not change the standing recommendation to keep the deterministic path as the submission default. The value of this experiment is a definitive, mechanistic root-cause explanation for a previously unexplained regression (closing the Priority 1 investigation in improvement_roadmap.md) plus a reusable, documented, zero-risk-by-default tuning knob (--dense-rrf-weight, default 1.0) for anyone continuing router work.
